verdict.rationale: WorkOS Directory Sync supports SCIM and sends automatic updates for changes to directories, groups and users. IT contacts can activate and deactivate accounts, and updates arrive via webhooks or the Events API. Customers praise its SCIM setup. However, the evidence does not show that deactivation in the IdP automatically revokes app access or sessions; the app appears to have to consume the events and enforce revocation itself. missing for 10: documented end-to-end deprovisioning that revokes active sessions or app access, explicit user-deleted/deactivated event semantics, independent hands-on corroboration of deprovisioning timing.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can sync users and groups from customer directories via SCIM so deprovisioning in the IdP revokes app access

citations.quote: WorkOS supports dozens of integrations including SCIM. Directory updates can be delivered to you via webhooks or retrieved using the Events API.
Directory Sync sends automatic updates to your app for changes to directories, groups, users, or access rules.
Directories enable IT contacts to activate and deactivate accounts, create groups that inform access rules
